stem.en: A car of mass 1200 kg starts from rest. Its velocity rises steadily to 12 m/s in 6 s. What is the net force on the car, in newtons?

explanation.en: a = (12 m/s - 0) / 6 s = 2 m/s². F = ma = 1200 kg x 2 m/s² = 2400 N, in the direction of motion.

correctFeedback.en: Correct — a = (10 − 0) ÷ 5 = 2 m/s², then F = ma = 1500 × 2 = 3000 N.

incorrectFeedback.en: Two named errors are common here. If you got 15000, you likely used the given velocity (10) directly as if it were the acceleration, skipping the a = (v − u) ÷ t step. If you got 750, you may have divided instead of multiplied, or divided by 2t instead of finding a first, then multiplying. Work it in two clean steps: first a = (v − u) ÷ t, then F = m × a — don't try to combine them into one calculation.

hints.en: Find a = (v - u) / t first, then use F = ma.
